description: Governance providers reach the gate they configure (PROTOCOL_SPEC 6.6.5.4, decision D-129). An ACL, ApprovalHandler or ExecutionPolicy given to an Executor MUST be bound into the built-in gate step of the RUNNING strategy, however that strategy was supplied -- by preset name, by default, or as a pre-built strategy instance -- and governance_state() MUST report the provider the running gate step actually holds. Before D-129 an explicit strategy instance received none of the executor's providers: a deny-all ACL let every call through while governance_state() reported acl_configured and builtin_acl_gate_wired as true.

driver_contract.path: Construct a real Executor through the public constructor, register the module `demo.target` (a trivial module returning {"ok": true}), make one real call as caller `@external` (no caller_id), then read governance_state(). Asserting only governance_state() is not enough: the defect this fixture pins is a call that RAN while the accessor said a gate stood in front of it.
driver_contract.strategy_form: `preset:standard` -- pass the preset NAME. `preset:internal` -- pass the `internal` preset name (acl_check and approval_gate removed). `instance:bare` -- build the standard strategy with the SDK's public builder WITHOUT passing any provider, then pass that instance to the Executor. `instance:own_acl` -- build the standard strategy passing `strategy_acl` to the builder, then pass the instance. `default` -- pass no strategy.
driver_contract.providers: `executor_acl` / `strategy_acl`: `deny_all` = an ACL with no rules and default_effect deny; `allow_all` = one rule callers ["*"] targets ["*"] effect allow, default_effect deny; null = none. `approval_handler`: `always_deny` = the SDK's AlwaysDenyHandler; null = none. `policy_strict`: true = ExecutionPolicy(strict=true) passed to the Executor.
driver_contract.expected: `call` is `ok` (the call returned {"ok": true}) or the error_code the call raised. `governance` lists the governance_state() fields asserted; fields not listed are not asserted by that case.

test_cases.note: The D-129 defect: a pre-built instance never received the executor's ACL, and the call ran.
API argument beats the provider already on the step (same precedence as set_acl()).
The step enforces an ACL the executor was never given; governance_state() MUST report what the running gate holds, not the executor field.
No handler, strict policy: the gate MUST fail closed, which it can only do if the policy reached the step.
Unchanged semantics: configured but not wired is reported as such, and the call runs.
